prerequisites: Basic knowledge in the area of Graphic Engineering, at University Access Exam level.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for critical thinking and self-criticism.
Ability to learn to work autonomously.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Capacity for spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Know the representation systems commonly used for solving problems in the technical field.
Acquire the ability to interpret a technical drawing.
Know the existence of regulations related to graphic representation in the technical field, and apply some of them.
Know the operational systematic of computer-aided design programs.
Apply acquired knowledge to the graphical resolution of problems.
Apply acquired knowledge to the preparation of construction or workshop drawings.

teaching_methods: Learning based on solving theoretical problems
Multimedia material with explanations on theoretical content
Multimedia material with theoretical problem solving

assessment_methods.method: Practical problem: Descriptive Geometry. Contoured Planes System
Practical problem: Descriptive Geometry. Dihedral System
Practical problem: Standardization and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is obtained as a weighted average from three practical problems (Block 1: 2/5, Block 2: 2/5, Block 3: 1/5). Each exercise is evaluated from 0 to 10 points. A minimum score of 3.5 points in each block is required for the average to be calculated, and the minimum overall average to pass the subject is 5 points. For the extraordinary call, students must be examined on all thematic blocks not passed (score less than 5) in the ordinary call. Scores of 5 or more from the ordinary call are retained, but students may retake passed parts to improve their grade, with the last score considered. For students authorized for a single final evaluation, 100% of the final grade is achieved through a single test consisting of three practical problems, following the same weighting and minimum score criteria.
